Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **ready‑to‑run Bash script** you can drop into your terminal (or put into a `.sh` file) that walks through every step you listed.  
Feel free to copy‑paste it line‑by‑line; I’ve added comments so you know what each block does.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

#########################
# 1️⃣ Clone the repo
#########################
REPO_URL="git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git"
TARGET_DIR="nodejs-welcome"

echo "Cloning $REPO_URL ..."
git clone "$REPO_URL" "$TARGET_DIR"

cd "$TARGET_DIR"

#########################
# 2️⃣ Analyse & scaffold
#########################

# 2.1 Create/update Dockerfile -------------------------------------------------
cat >Dockerfile <<'EOF'
# Base image – lightweight Node runtime
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

# Set working dir inside container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy only the metadata first – speeds up caching
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies (only production ones)
RUN npm ci --omit=dev

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Build step (if you have a build script)
# RUN npm run build

# Final stage – keep image small
FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /app ./

EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
EOF

echo "✅ Created Dockerfile"

# 2.2 Generate Kubernetes YAML -----------------------------------------------
mkdir -p deploy
cat >deploy/k8s.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/your-org/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with real registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to NodePort/ClusterIP as needed
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80                 # Service port exposed to cluster
    targetPort: 3000         # Container port
EOF

echo "✅ Generated Kubernetes manifests at deploy/k8s.yaml"

# 2.3 Add GitHub Actions workflow ---------------------------------------------
mkdir -p .github/workflows
cat >.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml <<'EOF'
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '18'

    - name: Cache npm modules
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: ~/.npm
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-npm-

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test || true   # If you don't have tests, remove or comment out

    - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: \${{ github.actor }}
        password: \${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build Docker image
      run: |
        IMAGE_NAME=ghcr.io/\${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome
        TAG=\${GITHUB_SHA::7}
        docker build -t \$IMAGE_NAME:\$TAG .
        docker tag \$IMAGE_NAME:\$TAG \$IMAGE_NAME:latest

    - name: Push Docker image
      run: |
        IMAGE_NAME=ghcr.io/\${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome
        TAG=\${GITHUB_SHA::7}
        docker push \$IMAGE_NAME:\$TAG
        docker push \$IMAGE_NAME:latest
EOF

echo "✅ Added GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml"

#########################
# 3️⃣ Stage all changes
#########################
git add -A
echo "✅ Staged all new/updated files"

#########################
# 4️⃣ Commit & push
#########################
COMMIT_MSG="CI/CD scaffolding: Dockerfile + K8s + GitHub Actions"
git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG"
git push origin main

echo "✅ Committed and pushed changes to main"
```

---

### What the script does

| Step | Action | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `git clone …` | Pulls the repo locally | Uses SSH; make sure your machine has an SSH key added to GitHub |
| `cat >Dockerfile …` | Creates a multi‑stage Dockerfile | Uses `node:18-alpine`, copies only `package*.json` first for cache efficiency |
| `mkdir -p deploy && cat >deploy/k8s.yaml …` | Writes a single `k8s.yaml` containing both Deployment & Service | Replace `ghcr.io/your-org/...` with your actual registry & image name |
| `mkdir -p .github/workflows && cat >.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml …` | Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that builds, tests, tags, and pushes the image | Requires the `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret (provided automatically); if you want to push to Docker Hub instead, swap the login/action section |
| `git add -A` | Stages everything | Includes the newly created Dockerfile, k8s.yaml, and workflow |
| `git commit -m … && git push origin main` | Commits and pushes | Make sure you’re authenticated (`ssh-agent` or HTTPS credentials) |

---

### After running the script

1. **Verify the files**  
   ```bash
   ls -R
   ```
   You should see `Dockerfile`, `deploy/k8s.yaml`, and `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml`.

2. **Check the GitHub Actions tab**  
   Once the push completes, navigate to *Actions* → *Build & Push Docker Image* → *Run workflow* → *View logs* to confirm the job succeeded.

3. **Deploy to a cluster**  
   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f deploy/k8s.yaml
   ```

4. **Expose the service**  
   If you’re using Minikube or kind, you might need to set `type: NodePort` or use `minikube tunnel`. For a cloud provider, `LoadBalancer` will provision an external IP.

---

#### Quick sanity check

If you just want to test the Dockerfile locally before committing:

```bash
docker build -t nodejs-welcome-test .
docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --name nodejs-welcome-test nodejs-welcome-test
curl http://localhost:3000   # Should hit your welcome endpoint
```

That’s it! Drop the script into your terminal, tweak the placeholders (registry names, image tags), and you’ll have a fully automated CI/CD pipeline plus ready‑for‑cluster manifests—all in one go.
